artists.biography:
The Clash were an English punk rock band that formed in 1976 as part of the original wave of British punk. Along with punk, their music incorporated elements of reggae, ska, dub, funk, rap, dance, and rockabilly. For most of their recording career, the Clash consisted of Joe Strummer (lead vocals, rhythm guitar), Mick Jones (lead guitar, vocals), Paul Simonon (bass guitar, vocals) and Nicky "Topper" Headon (drums, percussion). Headon left the group in 1982, and internal friction led to Jones's departure the following year. The group continued with new members, but finally disbanded in early 1986.

The Clash achieved commercial success in the United Kingdom with the release of their debut album, The Clash, in 1977. Their third album, London Calling, released in the UK in December 1979, brought them popularity in the United States when it came out there the following month. It was declared the best album of the 1980s a decade later by Rolling Stone magazine.

The Clash's politicised lyrics, musical experimentation and rebellious attitude had a far-reaching influence on rock, alternative rock in particular. They became widely referred to as "The Only Band That Matters", originally a promotional slogan introduced by the group's record label, CBS. In January 2003, the band-including original drummer Terry Chimes-were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. In 2004, Rolling Stone ranked the Clash number 28 on their list of the 100 greatest artists of all time.

perplexity.description:
The World According to The Clash is a career-spanning compilation that gathers 11 of the band’s most celebrated songs. Originally circulated in 1982 as a promotional radio LP without the group’s authorization, it has been officially reclaimed with new artwork and a revised selection that includes “The Magnificent Seven,” added at Mick Jones’s request. The track list moves from the hard-driving “Rock the Casbah,” “Clampdown,” and “Brand New Cadillac” to the politically charged “Spanish Bombs,” “The Guns of Brixton,” and “London Calling.”

As a concise introduction to The Clash’s restless fusion of punk, rockabilly, reggae, funk, pop, and early hip-hop influence, the collection reflects both their musical range and cultural reach. “Train in Vain,” “Lost in the Supermarket,” “I Fought the Law,” and “Should I Stay or Should I Go” complement the more overtly political material, highlighting the band’s gift for melody as well as confrontation. The 2026 Sony Music edition presents this historically unusual compilation as a limited orange-vinyl LP, making it particularly appealing to collectors and longtime fans.
